fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Chewing the cud is only half of it. The text says, “The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.” (Leviticus 11:4) One sign by itself doesn't get an animal on the list. I once tried to bake with only the chocolate chips and called it a batch.

Grass is a fair guess, friend, and I bet a lot of folks went right to it. But the verse never mentions grass. It says the pig “…does not chew the cud…” (Leviticus 11:7) The pig walks up with one sign, a split hoof, and the cud is the one it left at home. That's the word you want.

Yes, hopping! The exception is for flying insects “…having jointed legs above their feet for hopping on the ground.” (Leviticus 11:21) Then verse 22 names the kinds: locust, katydid, cricket and grasshopper. So the same bugs I'd swat off my cookie cooling rack are the ones this verse lists as okay to eat. Well, the text says it, friend, not me.
